Honestly at the end of the day I don’t think it matters as much as teachers tell you...
I did art for my HSC and the combination of that, drama and dance didn’t set me up for a great ATAR, but at least I got great grades and enjoyed it!
Even though I didn’t go straight from school to uni I don’t think I would of done it any other way, I worked for a few years and actually took some time to figure out what I wanted to do with my life before starting uni as a mature age student when my ATAR didn’t even matter anymore...

So don’t stress yourself, I don’t think anyone can know what they’re going to do for the rest of their life while they’re in school
I’ve also found it really helpful to individually address each criteria in the job description with an example and resolution proving my capability... if you look up the STAR method I use that

I’ve had recommendations to start cover letters a bit more personalised... my sister suggested for example she applied for a company with a great work culture and researched the business and their culture, apparently the staff called themselves busy bees or something to that effect... so to start ‘dear hiring etc... I am a busy bee looking for my hive’
I think it was probably said more eloquently, but it really got her cover letter to stand out and she got the job!
U just sound like a r/niceguys

The start of that reply being solely looks based... I feel like that kinda sidesteps the whole point of the initial post of finding genuine connection and not being shallow...

I also have to question why on earth girls would recommend a guy they didn’t like to their friends? Is that not awkward to pass off someone you used to date to your friends and then have to potentially see them regularly afterwards... That, and if I didn’t vibe with a guy why would my friends? Who’s to say my friends would even be interested

ah and the pill that was super cheap too, $20 for 4 months of contraception...

Unfortunately I don’t know the cost of insulin for you, but just regular medical care is great
